source.title: Proven Safety Countermeasures
source.publisher: Federal Highway Administration, U.S. Department of Transportation
source.terms: U.S. federal government work (17 U.S.C. 105). Free to use.
source.retrievalNote: The FHWA site refused automated download on 2026-10-13 (HTTP 403), as did the CMF Clearinghouse (certificate error). Each name and URL below was confirmed from web search results that returned that FHWA page; crash types summarize those results. [VERIFY] each entry against the live FHWA page before a plan is published.

listNote: FHWA groups its list into speed management, pedestrian and bicyclist, roadway departure, intersections, and crosscutting items. This file carries 14 of them. [VERIFY] the current FHWA count and any items added since the 2021 update.
cmfPolicy: A crash modification factor is shown only with its CMF Clearinghouse ID, after that entry has been read. No entry was read for this version, so every value is left out and marked [VERIFY].

countermeasures.name: Leading Pedestrian Interval
countermeasures.addresses: Pedestrian crashes with turning vehicles at signalized intersections.
countermeasures.cmfNote: [VERIFY] No CMF Clearinghouse entry read; no value given.

countermeasures.name: Road Diets (Roadway Configuration)
countermeasures.addresses: Rear-end and left-turn crashes on four-lane undivided roads, and long pedestrian crossings.
countermeasures.cmfNote: [VERIFY] No CMF Clearinghouse entry read; no value given.

countermeasures.name: Medians and Pedestrian Refuge Islands in Urban and Suburban Areas
countermeasures.addresses: Pedestrian crashes where people cross multilane urban and suburban roads.
countermeasures.cmfNote: [VERIFY] No CMF Clearinghouse entry read; no value given.

countermeasures.name: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
countermeasures.addresses: Pedestrian crashes at uncontrolled marked crosswalks.
countermeasures.cmfNote: [VERIFY] No CMF Clearinghouse entry read; no value given.

countermeasures.name: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons
countermeasures.addresses: Pedestrian crashes at midblock and other uncontrolled crossings.
countermeasures.cmfNote: [VERIFY] The FHWA page cites CMF Clearinghouse entries for this item, but none was read here; no value given.

countermeasures.name: Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements
countermeasures.addresses: Pedestrian crashes at crosswalks where drivers cannot see people crossing.

countermeasures.name: Roundabouts
countermeasures.addresses: Fatal and injury crashes at intersections, by removing high-speed angle and turning conflicts.

countermeasures.name: Appropriate Speed Limits for All Road Users

countermeasures.addresses: Speeding-related crashes where speeding is a demonstrated problem.
